plan: This is effectively a second-price sealed-bid auction (via the ascending clock mechanism), since the winner pays the second-highest bid, not their own. In such auctions, bidding your true value is the dominant strategy—it maximizes expected profit regardless of other bidders' strategies. Overbidding risks winning at a loss; underbidding risks losing profitable opportunities. Therefore, I will bid exactly my private value of $32.

Since this is effectively a second-price auction (the clock stops when the second-highest bidder exits at their sealed bid, and the winner pays that price), the dominant strategy is to bid exactly my true value. Bidding higher risks paying more than the item is worth to me if I win; bidding lower risks losing profitable opportunities. Therefore, I will bid $6, my true value, to maximize expected profit.

Since the sealed bid acts as my exit price in an ascending clock auction (equivalent to a second-price auction), bidding my true value is the dominant strategy. This ensures I win whenever my value exceeds the others' bids, paying only the second-highest bid, maximizing expected profit without risk of overpaying.
